update description: Needs identification must now precede all project proposals with structured digital scanning for existing data and explicit operational feasibility analyses, considering digital, AI, and automation capabilities from the outset. System enhancements or new data collections must be justified by documented inability to fulfill requirements with existing assets.
impact reasoning: This update changes the role from primarily responding to defined subject-matter and system requirements into a more upstream, evidence-based role in the enterprise intake process. Before proposing or implementing a new processing system, application, or data collection approach, the officer will be expected to conduct structured scans of existing data assets, metadata, systems, and reusable components, and to document whether the requirement can be satisfied through existing assets, automation opportunities, or digital workflow redesign. Feasibility work will become more standardized and formalized, incorporating cost-benefit-risk considerations, AI and automation readiness, digital interoperability, and sustainability factors. This increases the role's responsibility for enterprise alignment, documentation quality, and decision support at project initiation, not just during system development. The work-description would therefore shift from emphasizing technical development and feasibility in a narrower system context to emphasizing enterprise discovery, documented option analysis, asset reuse, and formal business-case support before development begins.

It would be updated to include a mandatory pre-development stage in which the officer scans existing enterprise data assets, systems, and reusable digital tools to determine whether requirements can be met without creating a new solution. Development work would proceed only after documented justification and feasibility review.

update description: Output objectives and any supporting system or operational plan must be justified for re-use, automation, and interoperability at inception. impact reasoning: This update changes the role from primarily assessing subject-matter and technical fit to conducting a broader gatekeeping and design-assurance function at the start of initiatives. The EC-04 must now evaluate whether proposed processing changes align with enterprise digital standards, can reuse existing data/assets, can be automated, and can interoperate with broader organizational systems before recommending development. The role shifts away from accommodating bespoke or manual approaches unless a documented exception is justified. This adds stronger responsibility for upfront challenge, documentation of rationale, and negotiation with subject-matter and IT stakeholders around constraints, reuse options, and resource discipline. Operationally, project initiation, specification development, and modification assessments become more structured and evidence-based, with greater emphasis on digital supply chain standards and justification frameworks.

update description: Initial identification of concepts shifts from iterative, expert-driven development toward system-guided exercises using AI and metadata. impact reasoning: This update changes the role from primarily originating subject-matter concepts and definitions for a specific program toward reviewing, arbitrating, and aligning concepts within enterprise metadata and interoperability frameworks. The work-description currently emphasizes developing concepts, proposing methods, and negotiating procedural changes largely from a subject-area and system-development perspective. Under the updated model, the EC-04 will still apply subject-matter expertise, but more often in validating AI-supported concept proposals, assessing fit with enterprise standards, documenting exceptions, and resolving cross-program conflicts. Operationally, this introduces faster review cycles, stronger reliance on metadata repositories and automated discovery tools, and greater participation in horizontal governance and standardization activities. The role evolves toward enterprise alignment, concept stewardship, and exception management rather than stand-alone conceptual authorship.
